newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: PSC to build 200,000 DWT shipyard.
newsitem.headline: PSC to build 200,000 DWT shipyard.

text.p: PSC Industries Bhd said on Monday it had submitted a proposal to the Malaysian government to build a shipyard in southern Johor state with an expected ship building capacity of 200,000 deadweight tonnes (DWT).

"It will be a totally new shipyard to be owned by all the shipyard companies in Malaysia. The capacity will be up to 200,000 DWT," Amin Shah Omar Shah, PSC chairman told reporters following the company's annual general meeting.
Amin Shah said the shipyard would be built by a consortium of local shipyard operators. "PSC will lead the consortium if possible," he said.
He did not identify the members of the consortium.
However, he said that he was open for the state government of Johor to participate in the equity of the proposed project. He declined to forecast the cost of the project.
One aim for the shipyard is to help reduce Malaysia's trade deficit, Amin Shah said. Several Malaysian shipping companies are acquiring ships from overseas, he noted.
Currently, vessels being ordered were between 3,000 and 150,000 DWT, so the proposed shipyard could build bigger ships, he noted.
In addition, over 60 percent of the vessels worldwide are over 25 years old. "They are coming to a time when they would need to be replaced," he said.
He added, however, that the new shipyard would extend ship building capacity in Malaysia and would not directly compete with existing domestic shipyards.

PSC, a shipbuilder, has 1 billion ringgit in orders to fulfill within three years, he said. The company is bidding for an additional 800 million to 1 billion ringgit worth of projects both locally and abroad, he said.
